brief.audience: City adults who have never tried ceramics

cases.question: Can a user get from a URL to a copyable fix prompt and back to a new score?
cases.why: This is the whole product. If any step breaks, nothing else matters.
cases.expected: Every step loads, at least one fix is offered, a prompt appears, the rerun shows up in the history, and the browser logs no errors.

cases.question: When a site gets fixed, does Better's score go up?
cases.why: The promise to users: apply our fixes, see your score improve. Uses the built-in demo site, which has a broken version and a fixed version.
cases.expected: After the fix, the sideways-scroll and small-text checks pass and the phone score goes up.

cases.question: Does Better notice tiny, messy text?
cases.why: Same page twice. One has tiny text in a dozen sizes, the other is clean. If Better can't tell them apart, its typography advice is noise.
cases.expected: The page with tiny, messy text gets fewer Typography points and a lower total than its clean twin.

cases.question: Does Better catch text that's too faint to read?
cases.why: Low contrast is an accessibility deal-breaker. Elle's rubric caps any site that fails it at 49 out of 100.
cases.expected: Faint text trips the contrast deal-breaker on the broken page only, and the broken page gets the lower total.

cases.question: Does Better notice a cluttered, everything-at-once page?
cases.why: Clutter is the most common problem with AI-built sites. Better should mark down hierarchy and information density.
cases.badLabel: Planted problem: clutter, no focal point
cases.expected: The cluttered page gets fewer Hierarchy and Information density points and a lower total.

cases.question: Does Better notice a page that only breaks on phones?
cases.why: This page looks fine on a laptop but scrolls sideways on a phone. Better should score the phone view lower instead of copying the desktop score.
cases.expected: The sideways-scroll check fails on the phone only, the phone deal-breaker trips, and the phone view scores lower.

cases.question: Does the same unchanged page get the same score every time?
cases.why: If scores wobble on their own, users can't tell whether their fix helped. Target: within 2 points.
cases.expected: Three runs on the same page land within 2 points of each other, with no failed AI calls.

cases.question: Does Better refuse to scan a private network address?
cases.why: Security: Better must never be usable to poke at internal networks.
cases.expected: Better refuses before scanning, with a clear message.

cases.question: When a site can't be reached, does Better say so instead of making up a score?
cases.why: A made-up score would destroy trust in every other score.
cases.expected: Better says the site could not be reached and shows no score.

cases.question: How does Better rate real public sites? (Tracked over time, not pass or fail.)
cases.why: A polished site (Stripe) should beat a famously chaotic one (Arngren).

brief.task: Learn who Yitzy is and get in touch

cases.expected: Recorded only. The polished site (Stripe) should score above the chaotic one (Arngren).
